info.name: Sub-Group-3C-Product-Inventory-API
info.description:
## Product Inventory API

This collection covers the core endpoints for managing a **product inventory system**, running locally at `localhost:4000`. It is designed to support full lifecycle management of products — from creation and retrieval to updates, deletions, and inventory monitoring.

### Endpoints Included

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/products/:id` | Retrieve details of a single product by ID |
| `POST` | `/products` | Create a new product with full details (name, brand, category, price, quantity, serial number, warranty, and low-stock threshold) |
| `PATCH` | `/products/:id` | Partially update an existing product's fields |
| `PUT` | `/products/:id` | Fully overwrite an existing product record |
| `DELETE` | `/products/:id` | Remove a product from the inventory |
| `GET` | `/products/low-stock` | Retrieve products that have fallen below their defined low-stock level |
| `GET` | `/products/warranty-expiring` | Retrieve products with warranties expiring within a given period |
| `GET` | `/products/warranty-expiring?days=7` | Test a custom warranty expiry period using query parameters |

### Key Features

- **CRUD operations** for individual product records
    
- **Inventory alerts** — identify products running low on stock
    
- **Warranty tracking** — monitor products with upcoming warranty expirations, including support for custom date ranges

request.description:
Retrieves the full details of a single product by its unique ID.

The product ID is specified as a path parameter in the URL (e.g., `/products/3`). A successful response returns all stored fields for that product, including its name, brand, category, price, quantity, serial number, warranty expiry date, and low-stock threshold.

Use this request to look up a specific product record in the inventory.

Retrieves a list of all products whose current quantity has fallen at or below their defined low-stock threshold.

No parameters are required. The API compares each product's `quantity` against its `lowStockLevel` and returns only those that need restocking.

Use this request to monitor inventory levels and identify products that require replenishment.

Retrieves a list of products whose warranties are expiring within the default upcoming period defined by the API.

No parameters are required for this request. The server evaluates each product's `warrantyExpiry` date and returns those falling within the threshold window.

Use this request to get a quick overview of products with upcoming warranty expirations, helping to plan maintenance or replacement actions.

Retrieves products whose warranties are expiring within a custom number of days, specified via the `days` query parameter.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `days` | integer | The number of days from today within which warranties must expire to be included in the results |

For example, setting `days=7` returns all products with warranties expiring within the next 7 days. This allows flexible, time-scoped warranty checks beyond the default period.

Use this request to test or fine-tune the warranty expiry window for specific operational needs.

Creates a new product entry in the inventory.

The request body must be sent as JSON and include all required product fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Full product name |
| `brand` | string | Manufacturer or brand |
| `category` | string | Product category (e.g., Laptop, Mouse) |
| `price` | number | Unit price |
| `quantity` | integer | Current stock quantity |
| `serialNumber` | string | Unique serial number for the product |
| `warrantyExpiry` | string (YYYY-MM-DD) | Warranty expiration date |
| `lowStockLevel` | integer | Quantity threshold that triggers a low-stock alert |

A successful response returns the newly created product record with its assigned ID.

Partially updates one or more fields of an existing product record without overwriting the entire entry.

The product ID is specified as a path parameter in the URL (e.g., `/products/2`). Only the fields included in the JSON request body will be updated — all other fields remain unchanged.

For example, sending `{ "quantity": 2 }` updates only the stock quantity for that product.

Use this request when you need to make targeted changes to a product, such as adjusting its price, quantity, or low-stock threshold, without resending the full product data.

Fully overwrites an existing product record with the data provided in the request body.

The product ID is specified as a path parameter in the URL (e.g., `/products/9`). Unlike a partial update, this request replaces the entire product entry — all fields must be included in the JSON body, as any omitted fields may be cleared or reset.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Full product name |
| `brand` | string | Manufacturer or brand |
| `category` | string | Product category |
| `price` | number | Unit price |
| `quantity` | integer | Current stock quantity |
| `serialNumber` | string | Unique serial number |
| `warrantyExpiry` | string (YYYY-MM-DD) | Warranty expiration date |
| `lowStockLevel` | integer | Low-stock alert threshold |

Use this request when you need to completely replace a product's data, such as during a bulk data correction or a full record refresh.

Permanently removes a product from the inventory by its unique ID.

The product ID is specified as a path parameter in the URL (e.g., `/products/10`). No request body is required. A successful response confirms the deletion of the product record.

Use this request to remove discontinued, duplicate, or incorrectly entered products from the inventory system. This action is irreversible — the product record cannot be recovered once deleted.
